title: The Manosphere Isn’t Ready for Brothercore
gist: Hey Brother House is a content incubator funded by a $180,000+ grant from the Young Men and Media Collective. It brings progressive-leaning male influencers together to copy the manosphere's editing style for "healthy masculinity" content. Wired's account of the Denver pilot shows strong bonding but a messy on-camera leadership conflict, 65-70 videos that mostly failed to reach 18-to-25-year-old men, and plans to scale to Austin and Atlanta with younger, less political creators.

insights.claim: Hey Brother House is a content incubator founded by Johnny Cole with Jonathan Jacobs and Matthew Echelman. A grant of more than $180,000 from the Young Men and Media Collective funds weeklong retreats meant to fill the social media feeds of 18-to-25-year-old men with healthy-masculinity content.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Philanthropic money now pays for creator content aimed at young men's feeds, a new kind of funded influencer marketing.
insights.locator: Cole, the founder of Hey Brother

insights.claim: Hey Brother House's playbook copies the manosphere's look (slick editing, dynamic hooks, fast montages) for wholesome content such as thrifting, golf and wrestling. It avoids lecturing and avoids mocking figures like Andrew Tate or Jordan Peterson, because attacking the messenger puts audiences on the defensive.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Counter-messaging that copies the format of what it opposes is a reusable approach to winning algorithmic distribution.
insights.locator: This is where the Hey Brother House comes in

insights.claim: Hey Brother House picked 8 creators from more than 130 applicants. They ranged from leftist commentators (Jerry Zeng, 133,000 Instagram followers; Ian Lightfoot, 1 million) to lifestyle and fitness influencers (Stephen Marmolejos, 180,000 TikTok followers, who does sponsored posts for Corona and Thayers). Chris Petrone (1.6 million TikTok followers) was among the most successful.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Mid-tier creators with brand sponsors are the delivery channel, so brand-safety and talent-manager incentives shape the content.

insights.claim: By 2023, clips of Andrew Tate had more than 13 billion views on social media. Wired attributes the manosphere's rise from a fringe movement to a major online force to influencers like Jordan Peterson and Tate, amplified by social media algorithms. Tate faces more than 40 criminal charges in the UK and Romania.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Platform algorithms reward the traditional-masculinity content that drives engagement, which is a reputational and regulatory risk for social platforms.
insights.quote: By 2023, clips featuring Tate had more than 13 billion views on social media platforms.

insights.claim: Johnny Cole argues that manosphere influencers profit from young men's insecurity by giving them a scapegoat and selling courses (such as drop-shipping) or paid 'alphas-only' men's circles.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: The manosphere is a creator economy built on paid courses, a revenue model built on audience grievance.

insights.claim: Young men are less likely than young women to finish high school and enroll in college. They are also dropping out of the job market and are more likely to report loneliness and to die by suicide.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Young men's disengagement from education and work matters over the long run for labor supply and political realignment.

insights.claim: Hey Brother House's Denver pilot produced 65 to 70 videos. The top performer, Mars Wright injecting testosterone while the others cheered, got 689,000 views. Wright's later 'Ask a Trans Man' series overperformed on Instagram and YouTube.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Content that is specific to one person's identity beat the generic bonding content, a lesson in what drives reach.

insights.claim: Little of Hey Brother House's content went viral or reached its target audience of men aged 18 to 25. Johnny Cole admits some was 'too on the nose' and says wrestling videos overperformed, so future content will tilt toward what young men want to see.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Openly ideological content struggles with the target audience. Distribution goes to entertainment-first formats.
insights.quote: There are some ways in which our content was too on the nose

insights.claim: A five-second looping Instagram Reel of Josh Kennedy and Johnny Cole hugging, captioned about getting a hug longer than 5 seconds, drew 500,000 views, mostly from 18-to-24-year-olds. It was the Denver house's clearest hit with Gen Z men.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Short, simple, emotionally direct loops can reach young men where explicit messaging fails.

insights.claim: Hey Brother House plans its next house in Austin in December and a third in Atlanta, with Colin Davis and Schuyler Bailar confirmed. Recruiting younger creators is hard: many are in school, talent managers don't want clients getting 'too political', and the house can't pay much.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Talent managers' aversion to political content and low pay limit how far grant-funded creator programs can scale.
insights.quote: A lot of them have talent managers who don’t want their clients to “get too political,”

insights.claim: A documentarian-led, on-camera 'tribunal' about founder Johnny Cole's leadership split the Denver house. Members said it felt like reality TV. Leaders now call the project a 'test-and-learn pilot' and are hiring a trained in-person men's group facilitator.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Leadership conflict and the pull of filming for the documentary are execution risks for creator-incubator models.

insights.claim: An estimated 67 percent of white male zoomers voted for Trump in 2024. One analysis of the November midterms found 54 percent of white men aged 18 to 29 voted for Democratic House candidates, a sharp swing left.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: A rapid swing in young men's votes suggests the manosphere's political pull may be fading, which matters for policy outlooks.
insights.quote: According to one analysis, 54 percent of this bracket voted for Democratic House candidates.

insights.claim: The Wired author sees signs that young men are tiring of older manosphere models of masculinity. She points to midterm wins by Abdul El-Sayed, James Talarico and Sen. Jon Ossoff, who offer a gentler model of masculinity.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: A cultural shift away from manosphere figures could weaken the engagement-driven creator economy around them.
